I like to analogize intelligence to penis size. The average penis size is something like 5.9in. Your perception of how large or small that is will be tinted by your experiences as well as how it's presented. If you've seen nothing but porn your entire life, 5.9in is going to seem quite small. If the possessor of the penis is quite overweight, the penis is going to seem much smaller, or if they have an inordinate amount of pubic hair, or are impotent, all of these things are going to affect your perception of their penis size. Stand side by side a very skinny man with a well trimmed bush and excellent blood flow and a very fat man with a veritable southern forest and a half-mast-at-best, one penis is going to seem MUCH larger, even if both are the same average 5.9in.

Intelligence is much the same. You could be the most brilliant person ever to live, but if you can't communicate, what good is it? If you have no memory, your range of convertible intelligence is quite low. If you have psychosis, depression, or some other behavioral disorder, or a substance use addiction, all of these things are going to dramatically affect your ability to convert and convey your natural intelligence into perceived, practical intelligence.

So, then, the question becomes, how might we measure practical intelligence? Very informally, I look for people who are quick and witty, who are funny (not just goofy or silly, but clever and fast), who are creative and can think of solutions to problems quickly, people who have mental fortitude, are resilient, can show the ability to think in different modes simultaneously (e.g. not just objective, critical thought, but also humanistic, gracious thought). I believe that people who are naturally intelligent, and have that intelligence buoyed up by excellent communication skills and a sharp memory are going to present as the smartest people in the room.
